en: Dependent on a cause that is both a *āsava* and a phenomenon, there arises a phenomenon that is neither a cause nor an *āsava*, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are five; ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance condition there are five.

Dependent on a cause that is not an *āsava*, there arises a phenomenon that is neither a cause nor an *āsava*, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are five; ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance condition there are five.

Conditioned by a phenomenon that is neither a cause but is an *āsava*, there arises a phenomenon that is neither a cause nor an *āsava*, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are three; ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance condition there are three.

Dependent on a cause that is free from the taints (*anāsava*), there arises a state that is neither a cause nor free from the taints by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under the root-condition there are three; under the predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*) there are three ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance-condition (*avigatapaccaya*) there are three.

Dependent on a cause that is associated with the taints (*āsavasampayutta*), there arises a state that is neither a cause nor associated with the taints by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root-condition there are nine; under the object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*) there are three ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance-condition there are nine.

Dependent on a root-conditioned state that is dissociated from the taints (*āsava*), there arises a state that is neither a root nor dissociated from the taints, by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under root [condition], three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance, three.

Dependent on a state that is both a root and associated with the taints, there arises a state that is neither a root nor associated with the taints, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition], five; ... pe ... under non-disappearance, five.

Dependent on a cause that is both with taints (*sāsava*) and not itself a taint (*anāsava*), there arises a state that is neither a cause nor a taint and is also not associated with taints, by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under the root-condition, there are five; ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance condition, there are five.

Dependent on a cause that is both with taints and associated with taints, there arises a state that is neither a cause nor a taint and is also dissociated from taints, by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root-condition, there are three; ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance condition, there are three.

Dependent on a non-root dhamma that is associated with the taints (*āsava*) but is not itself a taint, there arises a non-root dhamma that is dissociated from the taints and is not a taint, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Three under root; ... pe ... three under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a non-root dhamma that is dissociated from the taints but is subject to the taints (*sāsava*), there arises a non-root dhamma that is dissociated from the taints and is not subject to the taints, by way of root-condition. (Similar to the mundane.
Dependent on a root dhamma that is dissociated from the taints and is not a taint, there arises a non-root dhamma that is dissociated from the taints and is not a non-taint...

A state arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is not a root, dissociated from taints, and untainted, there arises a state that is not a root, dissociated from taints, and neither-tainted-nor-untainted, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is both a root and dissociated from taints and untainted, and a state that is not a root, dissociated from taints, and untainted, [there arises] a state that is not a root, dissociated from taints, and neither-tainted-nor-untainted... by way of root-condition.
A state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are three [answers] for root, three for predominance …pe… three for non-disappearance.
